plainTranslation: A's dreams meets B's love and values. The opposition pulls them into push-and-pull.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.

summaryDeep: Their idealism, vagueness, and dreams press against your affections, tastes, and sense of worth. It catches often enough that you both feel it, and it keeps asking to be worked out. Name it directly instead of letting it build in silence.
tension:
This is where the fog can go both ways. You may believe the other person is offering more than they have actually offered. They may believe you understood something they never clearly said. One person may become evasive because they do not want to disappoint. The other may become self-protective because the uncertainty starts to hurt. Before long, both people are responding to the story around the relationship, not the relationship itself.

In its shadow, Neptune can show up as unavailability, broken promises, vague intentions, not responding, avoidance, lying, or gaslighting. That does not mean this aspect predicts those behaviors. It means that when the bond begins with bliss and then becomes unclear, you have to name what is happening instead of explaining it away as romance.
advice:
Come back to what is actually happening between you. Not the story you have built around them. Not the future version of the relationship you hope will arrive. The person in front of you.

Longing can be powerful, but it is not the same thing as intimacy. The relationships that endure are not sustained by fantasy alone. They are built through the choices two people make to show up.
summaryShort: Their idealism, vagueness, and dreams press against your affections, tastes, and sense of worth.
